title: Subprocessor Notification and Model Provenance Procedure (template)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working template for (1) notifying customers and internal stakeholders when we add or materially change subprocessors involved in model weight storage, transfer, or model compilation, and (2) documenting provenance evidence required for any third-party model weights used in production. It combines a short customer-facing notice, an internal intake checklist, negotiator notes, and a sample contract clause that can be inserted into DPAs or vendor schedules.

Scope and triggers:
- Applies to any vendor/subprocessor engagement where the subprocessor will: store model weights, host checkpoints, perform model compilation/quantization, or otherwise have access to raw model artifacts used by Redwood to serve customer requests.
- Triggers: onboarding a new vendor; materially changing where model weights are stored or processed; onboarding a subcontractor beneath an existing vendor that meets the access conditions above.

Customer-facing notification (summary template):
- Subject: Notice of Subprocessor Change — Model Hosting/Compilation
- Body: "Dear customer,

We are notifying you that Redwood Inference expects to onboard (VendorName) as a subprocessor on (EffectiveDate). The subprocessor will provide (describe service: e.g., model weight storage in EU region / model compilation for quantization). We have evaluated the vendor and will impose the following controls: encrypted-at-rest keys managed in our KMS, access limited to named roles, periodic integrity checks, and an agreed retention schedule (RetentionPeriod). You may review the vendor security profile at (link) and raise objections within 30 days per Section X of your DPA.

Regards,
Redwood Inference Security & Compliance"

Internal intake checklist (SLA/Risk & legal):
- Vendor legal name and corporate entity used for contract.
- Data flows diagram showing: source model artifact origin, transfer paths, storage geolocations, and any ephemeral build hosts.
- Access model: which Redwood teams/roles and which vendor identities will have access.
- Crypto controls: KMS integration, HSM usage, envelope encryption scheme, key rotation frequency.
- Provenance evidence required: origin certificate for model weights, checksum manifest (SHA256), signed build logs for compilation steps, and a notarized supply chain manifest for any third-party binaries used.
- Audit rights: frequency and scope (on-site or remote), sample retention period for logs, and dedicated evidence handback procedure.
- Business continuity: SLAs for availability and RTO/RPO for artifacts.
- Data residency: confirm region constraints and any cross-border transfer exceptions.
- Vendor attestation: SOC2 type II (if available) + assignment of a named security contact.

Minimum provenance files to request from vendor (example):
- signed-manifest.json (contains file paths, SHA256 checksums, timestamps, and signing key id)
- compilation.log.gz (signed by vendor build account)
- manifest-signature.asc (PGP or PKCS#7 signature of manifest)
- binary-supply-list.txt (names and versions of toolchain components used during build)

Sample contract clause (short form for DPA/schedule insertion):
- Subprocessor Model Provenance and Records. Vendor shall provide, on request and within 10 business days, verifiable provenance artifacts for any model weight or compiled model that Redwood uses to serve Customer requests. Such artifacts shall include checksums, build logs, and cryptographic signatures sufficient for Redwood to validate origin and integrity. Vendor shall retain provenance evidence for a minimum of 24 months and shall permit Redwood or its designated auditor to access such evidence under the audit rights described in this Agreement.

Negotiator notes (things to push for):
- Timebound evidence handback (10 business days) and indemnity carveouts for provenance-related claims.
- Right to require re-compilation on Redwood-managed infrastructure if provenance cannot be validated.
- Explicit prohibition on vendor chaining (no subcontracting the storage/compilation without prior notice and independent attestation).
- Seek retention limits and hard-delete procedures for ephemeral build artifacts.

Escalation flow if provenance is incomplete or suspicious:
1) Create JIRA ticket (SEC-PROV-####) with summary and attach vendor manifest.
2) Security lead runs checksum validation and binary diff analysis; SRE helps rehydrate artifact in isolation.
3) If mismatch found, require vendor remediation plan (72 hours to acknowledge, 10 business days to remediate).
4) Notify affected customers per notification template; legal assesses contract remedies.

Operational considerations for SRE/Infra:
- Establish ephemeral build enclaves (air-gapped/cross-account) for vendor-provided compilation when we demand re-compilation.
- Automate SHA256 verification and signing of ingested artifacts; store provenance metadata in our evidence store with immutable timestamps.
- Monitor for unexpected changes to model sizes or tokenization metadata which can indicate tampering.

Open questions / negotiation levers (notes to self):
- What constitutes a "material" change that triggers customer notification for pre-existing customers? (propose: any change in geolocation, subprocessor identity, or where keys are held)
- Acceptable evidence formats (PGP vs PKCS#7) — lean to PKCS#7 for enterprise compatibility.
- Retention period alignment with customer DPAs (default 24 months, escalate to 36 months for regulated customers).

Appendix A — Example evidence exchange workflow (high-level):
1) Vendor uploads signed-manifest.json and compilation.log.gz to vendor S3 bucket with read-only pre-signed URL to Redwood.
2) Redwood orchestration downloads artifacts into isolated build account and runs verify_manifest.py which checks signatures and checksums.
3) On success, orchestration writes a provenance-record to internal evidence-store with a TTL-aligned retention tag and notifies Release Engineering.
4) On failure, security team opens remediation ticket and triggers customer notification flow.

Appendix B — Quick checklist for AE/CS when customers ask:
- Can we provide the vendor security profile? (link)
- Can vendor sign a subprocessor addendum? (yes/no)
- Who is the named security contact?
- What region will artifacts be stored/processed in?

Notes to future editors: keep this template short and modular. Move the sample clause into the standard clause bank in Confluence and reference it by id once finalized. This doc intentionally mixes customer-facing copy and internal steps because onboarding often requires parallel communication.

Unresolved items to validate with Legal:
- Standard indemnity language for compromise of provenance evidence.
- Whether we require notarized manifests for models trained by third parties.
- Standard timeline that we promise customers for notification (30 days vs 60 days).

End of template.
